title: Boss: a customer invoices API
summary: Issue API keys properly, then ship an API that authenticates them, stops BOLA, limits CORS and keeps keys out of its logs.

steps.title: The brief
body: A billing product exposes invoices to customers' own servers and to its web app. The security review asks for:
- API keys that are prefixed, random, stored hashed and shown masked
- every `/api` call authenticated; customers see only their own invoices, without internal fields
- CORS for the company's web app only
- logs that would survive being pasted into a public ticket

steps.title: API key lifecycle
prompt: - `(string Key, string StoredHash) Create(string environment)`: `environment` is `"live"` or `"test"` (else `ArgumentException`). The key is `dk_<env>_` + base64url of 32 random bytes; `StoredHash` is its SHA-256 as upper-case hex.
- `bool Matches(string presented, string storedHash)`: constant-time comparison of `Hash(presented)` with `storedHash`.
- `string Display(string key)`: the first 12 characters followed by `...` (or `****` for keys of 12 characters or fewer), for showing in a dashboard or log.
starter: public static (string Key, string StoredHash) Create(string environment) => ("", "");
public static bool Matches(string presented, string storedHash) => false;
solution: public static (string Key, string StoredHash) Create(string environment)
if (environment is not ("live" or "test")) throw new ArgumentException("environment must be live or test");
public static bool Matches(string presented, string storedHash) =>
public static string Display(string key) => key.Length <= 12 ? "****" : key[..12] + "...";
hints: `environment is not ("live" or "test")` guards the input.
template: Dojo.Check("live keys start with dk_live_", dojoKey.StartsWith("dk_live_"), dojoKey);
Dojo.Check("two keys differ", ApiKeys.Create("live").Key != dojoKey, "same key twice");
Dojo.Eq("the stored hash is SHA-256 hex", Convert.ToHexString(SHA256.HashData(System.Text.Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes(dojoKey))), dojoHash);
Dojo.Check("the stored hash isn't the key", dojoHash != dojoKey, "");
Dojo.Eq("Matches the right key", true, ApiKeys.Matches(dojoKey, dojoHash));
Dojo.Eq("doesn't match a near miss", false, ApiKeys.Matches(dojoKey[..^1] + "x", dojoHash));
Dojo.Eq("Display hides short values completely", "****", ApiKeys.Display("short"));

steps.title: The invoices API
prompt: Build it. **Run checks** starts the server and calls it.
- Two customers' keys (in the starter comments) stored as SHA-256 hashes. A middleware authenticates `X-Api-Key` for every path under `/api` (`401` otherwise) and records the customer.

- `GET /api/invoices` -> the caller's invoices as `[{"id", "amount"}]` (no `owner` field). `GET /api/invoices/{id}` -> `200 {id, amount}` for the caller's own invoice, `404` for anyone else's or a missing one.

- CORS policy: origin `https://app.example`, methods `GET` and `POST`, headers `X-Api-Key` and `Content-Type`. A browser preflight (`OPTIONS`) carries no key, so `UseCors` must run before your key middleware.

- The middleware appends a line per request to an in-memory log like `GET /api/invoices key=dk_live_ada_...` (first 12 characters of the key, or `none`). `GET /logs` (open, for the tests) returns the lines as a JSON array. The full key must never appear.
solution: var keys = new Dictionary<string, string>   // hash -> customer
var invoices = new List<Invoice> { new(1, "ada", 120m), new(2, "bob", 75m) };
var who = key.Length > 0 && keys.TryGetValue(Sha(key), out var customer) ? customer : null;
invoices.FirstOrDefault(i => i.Id == id && i.Owner == (string)ctx.Items["customer"]!) is Invoice inv
record Invoice(int Id, string Owner, decimal Amount);
hints: Hash the incoming key with SHA-256 hex and look it up in a dictionary of hashes.
`ctx.Request.Path.StartsWithSegments("/api")` limits the check to the API.
Project to `new { i.Id, i.Amount }` so `Owner` never leaves the server.
template: public static async Task Run(HttpClient http)
await Dojo.TryAsync("Authentication and BOLA could be checked", async () =>
DojoWeb.Status("no key gets 401", 401, await Send(http, "/api/invoices", null));
DojoWeb.Status("a wrong key gets 401", 401, await Send(http, "/api/invoices", "dk_live_ada_0000"));
var list = await DojoWeb.Json(await Send(http, "/api/invoices", Ada));
Dojo.Eq("ada lists only invoice 1", "1", list.ValueKind == JsonValueKind.Array ? string.Join(",", list.EnumerateArray().Select(i => DojoWeb.Prop(i, "id"))) : "(not an array)");
Dojo.Eq("and the owner field isn't exposed", null, list.ValueKind == JsonValueKind.Array && list.GetArrayLength() > 0 ? DojoWeb.Prop(list[0], "owner") : "(none)");
DojoWeb.Status("ada reads invoice 1", 200, await Send(http, "/api/invoices/1", Ada));
DojoWeb.Status("ada can't read bob's invoice 2 (404)", 404, await Send(http, "/api/invoices/2", Ada));
DojoWeb.Status("bob reads invoice 2", 200, await Send(http, "/api/invoices/2", Bob));
await Dojo.TryAsync("CORS could be checked", async () =>
Dojo.Eq("the app's origin is allowed", "https://app.example", pre.Headers.TryGetValues("Access-Control-Allow-Origin", out var v) ? string.Join(",", v) : null);
Dojo.Check("another origin isn't allowed", !er.Headers.Contains("Access-Control-Allow-Origin"), "Access-Control-Allow-Origin was sent");
await Dojo.TryAsync("The logs could be checked", async () =>
Dojo.Check("the logs mention the requests", logs.Contains("/api/invoices"), logs);
Dojo.Check("the logs show a key prefix", logs.Contains("dk_live_ada_"), logs);
Dojo.Check("no full key ever appears in the logs", !logs.Contains(Ada) && !logs.Contains(Bob), "a full key was logged");
static Task<HttpResponseMessage> Send(HttpClient http, string url, string? key)
if (key is not null) msg.Headers.Add("X-Api-Key", key);

steps.title: Structured log scrubbing
prompt: Structured logs are dictionaries, not lines. Write `Dictionary<string, string> Scrub(Dictionary<string, string> fields)` that returns a **new** dictionary where:
- a field whose name (ignoring case) is `authorization`, `cookie`, `set-cookie`, `password`, `client_secret`, `refresh_token`, `access_token` or `x-api-key` gets the value `[REDACTED]`;
- any other value that contains a JWT (`eyJ` + base64url, dot, base64url, dot, optional base64url) has each JWT replaced by `[JWT]`;
- everything else is copied unchanged. The input must not be modified.
hints: Build a new dictionary in a `foreach (var (name, value) in fields)` loop.
template: Dojo.Eq("a JWT inside text is masked", "replayed [JWT] twice", dojoOut.GetValueOrDefault("note"));
Dojo.Eq("the input is untouched", "Bearer abc", dojoIn["Authorization"]);
